issues.description: Fixed packetization pacing relies entirely on existing send-interval logic — no stated invariant or termination argument for the buffer
issues.detail: The new buffer accumulates bytes and drains in a while-loop, but there is no comment stating the invariant (len(buffer) < packet_bytes after drain) nor reasoning about how this interacts with _next_send_time. A literate comment naming the invariant and the pacing relationship would let a reader verify correctness without running the code.

issues.description: fixed_audio_packet_size has no validation; non-multiple-of-sample-width values silently produce broken PCM
issues.detail: PCM16 mono requires packet_bytes to be a multiple of 2 (and of frame size for the target codec). The code accepts any int. A misconfigured 641 will slice samples in half and produce noise. Either assert packet_bytes % sample_width == 0 at setup or document the constraint clearly.

issues.description: Resampler output assumed monotonic but no invariant stated for length divisibility
issues.detail: VonageFrameSerializer.serialize returns resampled bytes whose length depends on resampler internals. Combined with fixed_audio_packet_size buffering downstream, the system depends on length(resample(x)) being well-behaved. The contract of create_stream_resampler is not stated here; a one-line comment on what guarantees the buffer eventually drains would help.

issues.description: bytearray slice-and-del is O(n) per drain; with small packets and large payloads this is quadratic
issues.detail: del self._audio_send_buffer[:packet_bytes] shifts the remaining bytes each iteration. For typical 20ms@16kHz packets this is negligible, but if a serializer emits a large burst the inner while-loop is O(n^2) in buffer size. A memoryview or deque-of-chunks would be O(n). Not worth fixing without measurement — flagged for awareness.

issues.description: DTMF digit parsing has two fallback shapes with no documented source for either
issues.detail: digit = message.get('digit') or message.get('dtmf', {}).get('digit') accommodates two payload shapes 'in case'. A reader cannot tell which is the documented Vonage format and which is defensive. Cite the spec for the canonical shape and remove the speculative branch, or comment why both are observed.

issues.description: InterruptionFrame clears send buffer but resampler internal state is not reset
issues.detail: On interruption the byte buffer is cleared, yet self._output_resampler may carry state (filter history) from the dropped audio. If the resampler is stateful this produces a small artifact on the next utterance. Worth confirming the resampler is stateless across calls or adding a reset; either way state the invariant.

review.summary: The PR adds a Vonage serializer and a fixed-size audio packetization path on FastAPIWebsocketTransport. The algorithms are simple and likely correct, but the loop invariants for the new send-buffer drain and its interaction with pacing/interruption are not stated in comments — the code is UNDER-AUDITED rather than wrong. fixed_audio_packet_size accepts any int with no validation that it aligns with PCM sample width, which is a foot-gun. The bytearray drain is O(n^2) in the worst case but PREMATURE-OPTIMIZATION to fix without measurement at realistic packet sizes. Overall: NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT on the buffering contract, and one cheap precondition check on packet size.
